summary: Rob Carver and Niels review April 2025 for trend followers after Liberation Day and Rob's own 2024-25 drawdown year. Discussion of stops vs continuous sizing, drawdown maths, costs, a single-EMA trend paper, industry history and leveraged ETFs. Conclusion: bad years are normal for trend, process discipline matters, leveraged ETFs are toxic.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the TR US Treasury bond is a little bit like the the GI and good for the financial markets
claims.claim: US Treasuries have traditionally behaved like a Giffen good for markets: demand rises when risk and fear rise, making them the default safe haven.
claims.indicator: US Treasury bond demand in stress
claims.testable: partly - safe-haven behaviour of Treasuries in equity sell-offs can be tested

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: people temporarily at least didn't seem that keen on owning US Treasury bonds
claims.claim: In the April 2025 tariff shock Treasuries sold off alongside equities instead of acting as the go-to safe asset, unlike earlier crises.
claims.indicator: Treasury yield vs equity moves in the Liberation Day sell-off
claims.direction: Treasuries sold, no flight to safety
claims.conditions: crisis originating in the US / US policy uncertainty
claims.testable: yes - stock-bond correlation in stress episodes

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: something like a Swiss Franks uh seems to still be be um having that um uh ability
claims.claim: The Swiss franc still seems to retain safe-haven behaviour when Treasuries and the dollar do not.
claims.testable: yes - CHF return in equity drawdowns

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we are again just using kind of recency bias, meaning that we think about bonds as a safe haven because we've been in a 40-year cycle where interest rates just went down
claims.claim: Bonds' safe-haven reputation may be recency bias from a 40-year falling-rate cycle, and may not hold if rates trend higher.
claims.direction: bonds less protective in a rising-rate era
claims.testable: yes - stock-bond correlation by rate regime

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the policies of the US government seem deliberately designed to create stagflation
claims.claim: If policy produces stagflation (stagnation plus tariff inflation), the normal central bank reaction of cutting rates when growth weakens may not apply, so bonds hedge less.
claims.indicator: central bank reaction function under stagflation

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: maybe it's the Chinese and they want to actually punish the US government
claims.claim: Traditional Treasury buyers (e.g. China) may deliberately avoid Treasuries, and a crisis born in the US may make Treasuries a poor safe haven, a flows-based explanation.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I think the breakdown in kind of institutional frameworks and
claims.claim: Breakdown of institutional rules and frameworks is bad for US assets and markets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my trend barometer yesterday finished at 52, which actually is a good reading
claims.claim: Niels' CTA trend barometer reading of 52 at end of April 2025 coincided with a decent 10-day CTA recovery, though it is a short-term measure.
claims.testable: partly - barometer is a CTA-index derived gauge

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: MEI world index for example dropped 11% peak to trough and still it managed to end the month of April positive
claims.claim: April 2025 was a roller coaster: MSCI World fell 11% peak to trough yet ended the month positive, so CTAs caught on the wrong side of reversals after Liberation Day lost money.
claims.direction: trend followers lose on sharp V reversals
claims.testable: yes - trend returns around V-shaped reversals

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: more safe haven assets selling off like the dollar. uh we saw bonds got sold quite hard initially
claims.claim: Safe-haven assets (dollar, bonds) sold off in the shock, so dollar and Treasury trend positions were ineffective hedges in April 2025.
claims.direction: dollar and Treasuries fell with equities

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: returns in the range of say minus one or flat to about down 10% uh for the month
claims.claim: The largest trend followers lost from about 1% to 10% in April 2025, leaving year-to-date results between slightly up and down 15-18%.
claims.conditions: dispersion by speed, risk management and markets traded

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they're not unusual once you sort of uh look at it in historical perspective at least according to CFM
claims.claim: Dispersion of returns across trend followers is not unusual historically (CFM research); speed, risk management and markets traded are the usual sources of differentiation.
claims.testable: yes - compare manager dispersion over time

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Japanese government bonds uh copper silver those were actually specifically tricky markets
claims.claim: Single markets such as JGBs, copper and silver were specifically tricky for trend followers in April 2025, while short-term interest rates, softs and meats gave relief.
claims.indicator: JGB, copper, silver, short-term interest rates, softs, meats

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I thought this month particular could be quite different from whether you use a stop hard stop uh system or whether you use continuous signals
claims.claim: April 2025 outcomes may differ materially between hard-stop trend systems and continuous-signal systems.
claims.testable: yes - simulate both rule types on the episode

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: commodities really won the day again uh in April
claims.claim: Commodities (energies, grains) again delivered the trend-following gains in April, as in past stress periods.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: short-term models, certainly enjoyed uh the first half of the month better than the longerterm models
claims.claim: Short-term models gained more in the first half of April 2025 than long-term models, but later reversals erased much of that benefit and moves were sometimes too fast (overnight gaps) even for fast models.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: most people would have had um negative alpha from the portable side and and maybe the beta side actually ended up pretty flat
claims.claim: Portable alpha products (trend overlay on equity beta) had negative alpha and flat beta in April 2025, so looked bad though doing what they are designed to do.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I was down five and a half% maybe in line with the industry actually.
claims.claim: Rob's own April 2025 return was -5.5%, roughly in line with the industry; the very fastest models made a little money on the initial bounce but whipsawed afterwards.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: if you get stopped out and then you get this bounce and sometimes, you know, it's great to have, you know, a a simple trigger um and you're out and sometimes it works against you
claims.claim: A stop-based trend follower who is stopped out cannot re-enter until a new signal, so can miss the bounce, while a continuous-signal approach keeps participating.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the only way that would have been trading fast and also very, very fast indeed
claims.claim: Capturing the April 2025 V-shaped bounce would require extremely fast trading; trading only slightly too slowly gets whipsawed, while a very wide stop simply holds through.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if let's say you were running a stop loss trend following system but your stop was a bit tighter
claims.claim: A tight stop gets triggered near the lows, booking a loss and leaving a flat position, producing a sharp drop then flat P&L curve.
claims.conditions: tight stop with a ~18-20% drawdown trigger

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm running currently something like a third of my normal risk levels
claims.claim: Variable position sizing that adjusts positions daily to risk automatically cut Rob's risk to about a third of normal (less in equities) as the trend became unclear, so his P&L dropped then went sideways.
claims.testable: yes - compare dynamic sizing vs stops

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: running um with with variable position sizing essentially makes your distribution returns closer to a normal distribution to a nice bell curve without extreme outliers
claims.claim: Variable position sizing makes return distributions closer to normal with fewer extreme outliers, while stops make outliers (both big winners and big losers) more likely.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: you know, makes you more likely that you'll have a, you know, bigger outliers.
claims.claim: Stop-based systems give larger outliers; the upside outliers are desired for positive skew but downside outliers occur when closing at the wrong moment or when an oversized position (e.g. cocoa) moves against you.
claims.conditions: oversized exposure to a market that has run up

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: when you build up a lot of open profit which of course is great for the investors who are in the fund
claims.claim: Funds with large open profits after a big run (high flyers) risk large give-back, so new investors entering at that time face outsized drawdown risk, as seen in April 2025.
claims.conditions: new investor entering after a hot streak

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: in the bad years, you could be down 30 40 50 60% potentially
claims.claim: Funds that can make 100%+ in good years can lose 30-60% in bad years; whether that is Kelly-optimal matters less than whether investors can stomach it.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: SG trend down 4.98% um and down 9.41% for the year
claims.claim: April 2025 index results: Barclay BTOP50 -3.49%, SG CTA -4.47%, SG Trend -4.98% (-9.41% YTD), SG short-term traders -0.86%, Bridge flat-fee trend -6.24% (-10.58% YTD), MSCI World +0.74%, S&P 500 -0.68%, US aggregate bonds +0.36%.
claims.indicator: BTOP50, SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term Traders, Bridge alternatives index

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: The first quarter was so strong, the best I think it had was probably the best quarter in in the last 25 years.
claims.claim: Trend following had its best quarter in about 25 years in Q1 2024, then became much more challenging from April 2024.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: My worst my worst ever year of of since I started doing this with my own money which is my first full year was um April 2014 to April 2015.
claims.claim: Rob's worst year in his own trading was about -15%, a roughly one-in-10-year event; the 2024-25 tax year drawdown was driven by a few short sharp legs (about 12% over 3 weeks tied to the yen), not by a steady bleed.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: It's rarely because you're overexposed to one individual market
claims.claim: In a well-diversified multi-asset, multi-speed portfolio a bad year occurs because everything goes wrong at once, not because of concentration in one market; Rob lost money in equities, energies, FX, metals and bonds (but made money in S&P), with natural gas the worst.
claims.conditions: diversified trend portfolio in a trendless year

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the SGCTA index for for the period I looked at which was um end of March to end of March sorry it was down 10%
claims.claim: Over the year to end-March/April 2025 the SG CTA index was about -10% versus Rob at about -14.7% on much higher volatility, so vol-adjusted his performance was acceptable.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I think the dynamic is better at risk targeting so even if it doesn't give me extra return I'll probably stick with it
claims.claim: Selecting positions dynamically from a larger instrument universe shows noisy return differences year to year versus the earlier set, but gives better risk targeting, which is a reason to keep it.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: pretty much all of them uh lost money um apart from three which was um fast relative momentum relative car carry and relative value skew
claims.claim: Of about 50 forecasting variables, nearly all lost money over the year except fast relative momentum, relative carry and relative value skew; relative (cross-sectional) signals held up, and even carry (especially the slowest) lost, so style diversification helped.
claims.indicator: fast relative momentum, relative carry, skew value
claims.direction: relative signals worked while outright trend failed

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: mathematically um the the longer you run any trading strategy the worse the bigger your worst draw down will get over time
claims.claim: The longer a strategy runs, the larger its worst drawdown is expected to be, since expected worst drawdown grows with time, so veteran funds hitting new worst drawdowns is mathematically unsurprising.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: what's the probability of getting a draw down this size in say a 12 year trading period and it'll tell you that you know it's about a 30% chance
claims.claim: Compare the current drawdown to the probability of such a drawdown in a comparable period (about 30% over 12 years) rather than just to the backtest max; a 50% drawdown would be well beyond the backtest and expectation and be a real concern.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the sort of um efficacy of of of particularly trend following signals is quite low. The sharp ratio is not that high
claims.claim: Because trend signals have a modest Sharpe ratio, it takes a very long time to statistically tell that a strategy has stopped working, so continuing is largely a matter of faith.
claims.testable: yes - power analysis of Sharpe tests

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if things start to go against you as a systematic trader, in theory, you should do nothing, but in practice it's very hard not to
claims.claim: Systematic traders should in theory do nothing when a strategy underperforms; both managers and investors find this hard, and investors tend to redeem after bad months.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it was also the beginning of one of the best 12 months returns that they've ever had
claims.claim: November 2021 was one of the worst single days for many trend managers yet was followed by one of their best 12-month periods, so redeeming after a bad month can be wrong.
claims.indicator: trend follower returns after sharp drawdown days

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: whenever I've tried to do that in a quantitative way I found very few things that that sort of tell you whether a trend fun is going to do well or badly
claims.claim: Attempts to meta-time trend following with quantitative conditioning variables found very few useful predictors; best response is providing visibility by showing historical analogues where trend did fine.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I was just under um 100 basis points which is kind of in line with with what I expect in my back test
claims.claim: Rob checks commissions plus slippage annually (about 100 bp, in line with backtest) because costs are predictable while P&L is nearly random; slippage is the fill price versus mid at order time, and passive limit orders then switching give lower costs than the conservative half-spread backtest.
claims.indicator: trading cost and slippage vs mid

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I actually sold all my remaining US stock exposure
claims.claim: Rob, already underweight US stocks, sold remaining US stock exposure before Liberation Day and went to cash in his long-only portfolio, his biggest discretionary decision ever, outside his systematic portfolio.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: it feels like the US economy has kind of run out and it's just not realizing that there's there's nothing below it and it's just going to crash
claims.claim: Rob expects a deep technical US recession as tariffs hit goods already in transit; Q1 GDP was unaffected by tariffs, and CEOs are reluctant to give honest forward earnings, so the real-economy effect and earnings downgrades come later and the market should not stay where it is.
claims.indicator: US GDP, corporate earnings guidance, tariffs
claims.conditions: lags between tariffs and real-economy data

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: I'm now my money's in cash it's earning you know four 4% or something a year. Do I think the market's going to be 4% higher? I mean, maybe. But the risk is just astonishing.
claims.claim: Staying in cash at about 4% is preferred to equities whose expected return may only be about 4% given large downside risk; his systematic portfolio still follows trends, so he would partly benefit if equities rally.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there were some positions I couldn't sell. There was no bid in the
claims.claim: In the first days after Liberation Day some positions could not be sold because there was no bid, illustrating liquidity risk in stress.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the cost of having an additional signal in there is zero
claims.claim: Different trend indicators are highly correlated, so no one is uniquely best, but once automated the cost of adding another signal is zero, so you might as well include several.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: what if we were to just pick up one single indicator
claims.claim: A single calibrated exponential moving average can summarise the whole universe of trend indicators (a representative filter), using the mathematical link between exponential and simple moving averages.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: if you use um a just an explanatory moving average with 112 days as the parameter that's optimal at capturing trends
claims.claim: The paper reports an exponential moving average with a 112-day parameter is optimal at capturing trends; Rob would not replace his multi-indicator system but values it as first-principles thinking.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: there is a very fine balance between simplicity in your trend system and over complication and it's really about getting that balance right
claims.claim: There is a fine balance between simplicity and over-complication in trend systems and it makes a big difference.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: there's almost two or maybe even three sort of original parents or grandparents in this family tree
claims.claim: Trend followers form a family tree with distinct lineages (US pit-trading wing, British quantitative wing, Scandinavian), which explains differences of opinion about sizing and position changes.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Of course, we've survived many of those uh in the past. I'm not worried about
claims.claim: The question whether trend following is dead has recurred many times and the industry survived each time.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: By 2020, only a small part of Winton's flagship fund was in traditional trend following.
claims.claim: Winton diversified away from pure trend following into other quant strategies, did poorly when CTAs did well and was more correlated to equities, with AUM falling from above $30bn to $7.5bn, while Aspect stuck to trend and returned 40% in 2020.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Winon has really done a great job in rebuilding the trend side
claims.claim: Winton has rebuilt its trend-following allocation and again manages a lot of money there.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: he talks about the NASDAQ being up 7% every year, and if you have a 3x leveraged NASDAQ, um, ticker, you can make 21%
claims.claim: A tweet claims 3x leveraged Nasdaq turns 7% a year into 21%, which ignores that leveraged ETFs reset daily and are not a remotely good idea.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: So, it's lost over half its value.
claims.claim: The one quadruple-leveraged S&P 500 ETF was down 52% year to date versus S&P down about 4.5%, because daily reset compounding makes adverse moves devastating.

claims.speaker: Rob Carver
claims.quote: the expense ratio on that is a incredibly is 295 basis points
claims.claim: Leveraged ETFs carry high expense ratios (about 295bp) and are toxic as holding instruments; multiples of 2-4x on already risky assets exceed Kelly-criterion sizing.
claims.indicator: leveraged ETF expense ratio, Kelly criterion
